annotations.text:
FIVE DIRECTIONS — same screen, same data, five design languages.

All five are drawn from the real tokens: CA #00264A / #003A70 / #F2A900, the Google-blue brand ramp, the 3-column field grid.

What every one of them fixes, because all three are measured faults in the build today:

1. White toolbar text on the gradient's gold end sits at 2.0:1. AA wants 4.5:1.

2. 15 controls in one flat header row, destructive Clear PII at the same weight as Export JSON.

3. 174 red text nodes on a form nobody has touched — empty rendered as wrong.

Pick one and I build it across the whole app.

A · CIVIC MODERN — my pick

Keeps the government identity and executes it properly. The navy goes solid; the state colour becomes a 3px rule and a plate, so nothing interactive ever sits on a gradient. Actions drop to a white sub-bar in three labelled groups, Clear PII outlined rather than filled. Empty fields read as 'still to fill', amber only where a jurisdiction rule actually has something to say.

Trade-off: it is the safe one. Correct, legible, and nobody is going to gasp.

B · INSTRUMENT

Treats the payload as the product. Dark, dense, monospace. The field form becomes a table with a length column, and the right half becomes the byte ledger inspect.ts already computes and nothing surfaces — offsets, declared vs accounted, padding, unknown codes. State colour shrinks to a 3px bar. Fastest thing here for someone doing this all day.

Trade-off: cold. It drops the DMV character entirely, and a table is worse than cards on a phone.

C · LEDGER

Paper, not software. Warm ground, Newsreader for the display face, ruled entry lines instead of filled boxes, sections numbered §1 §2. Rules and type carry the hierarchy — no cards, no shadows. Calm on a screen you sit in front of for an hour.

Trade-off: lowest density of the five, so more scrolling. Serif numerals in a field of 8-digit dates need watching. And it reads more like a document than a tool.

D · KIOSK

The only one that changes structure rather than paint. One section at a time behind a step rail, 56px controls, 16–18px type. This is the direction that fixes the phone at the root: today 347px of an 844px iPhone screen is chrome before the first input. Optional fields are visibly dashed, so you can see what you may skip.

Trade-off: power users lose the whole-form view and Ctrl+F across all 32 elements. Biggest build of the five.

E · LAMINATE

Full commitment to the bit. Guilloche security print under everything, a rainbow sheen across the masthead, numbered form boxes set like a real paper application, Courier throughout. The preview stops being a floating barcode and becomes the card front, with the code where it actually sits.

Trade-off: loud, and it edges toward resembling the credential rather than a tool that makes one. Hardest of the five to keep accessible and the one most likely to wear thin.
